### Tank Dell caught 4-of-9 targets for 105 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.


The Texans seemed fairly comfortable using Dell in this one, getting him going with a screen pass on the opening drive. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard touchdown via a go route, in which he simply ran past his coverage defender down the right sideline. CJ Stroud hit Dell in stride and he continued on down the field and into the end zone. Dell managed to earn an end zone target on the Texans’ 11th drive, but was unable to secure it. Dell is officially on the WR3/FLEX radar for Week 10 against the Browns.

### NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.





“The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

- Texans Week 9 snap counts: How much did WR Tank Dell play in win over L.A. Chargers?


Cole Thompson, Texans Wire·Texans Wire

Mon, November 9, 2026 at 9:55 AM EST·

4 min read

Just like that, the [Houston Texans](https://texanswire.usatoday.com/) are back in the conversation for postseason chatter.

In his return back to Los Angeles, [C.J. Stroud](https://texanswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/texans/2026/11/09/houston-texans-qb-c-j-stroud-week-9s-win-vs-l-a-chargers-win-nfl-trade-deadline/92688889007/) threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as the [Texans](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/houston-texans/325) rolled past the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://texanswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/texans/2026/11/08/houston-texans-los-angeles-chargers-week-9-live-updates-nfl-trade-deadline-rumors--live/92679735007/) in a [44-22 victory](https://texanswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/texans/2026/11/08/texans-chargers-derek-stingley-first-interception-of-season/92682918007/) at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Advertisement

Stroud, who wanted to see an uptick in consistency after Week 7's overtime loss to the [New York Giants](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/new-york-giants/351), threw an early pick on a pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage. He missed Nico Collins on a third-down conversion and overthrew Marvin Harrison Jr. in the second quarter.

Outside of that, the former No. 2 overall pick looked like the quarterback that was promised back when drafted out of Ohio State in 2023. He connected with four different receivers, including twice with Kayshon Boutte for touchdown passes. Six passes went for gains of over 20-plus yards and were recorded as explosives.

The [Texans](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/houston-texans/325) punted with less than two minutes in the second quarter. Kai Kroeger would only take the field one more time for the rest of the afternoon.

For as good as Stroud was, the Texans' defense delivered a much-needed, jolt-worthy performance while attacking Justin Herbert. The Chargers' quarterback, who entered Sunday as the second-most-hit passer through eight weeks, took over at No. 1 as Houston's defense recorded a season-high eight sacks, including two each by Sheldon Rankins and Jadeveon Clowney.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Advertisement

Entering the third quarter, Los Angeles tried to get something moving in the passing game, but an interception by Derek Stingley Jr. stopped a chance for a scoring drive. On the flip side, Stroud found Nico Collins, who made an impressive one-handed catch for a 13-yard touchdown grab, only extending Houston's lead by 26.

But perhaps the best moment of the day came with Tank Dell's arrival back on the field. After missing nearly two seasons with a severe leg injury suffered in 2024, Dell didn't seem to miss a beat, hauling in four passes for 105 yards, including a 63-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter.

Below is a breakdown of the playing time from Sunday's win, including some separation at wide receiver, running back, tight end and a deeper rotation at linebacker.

## Offense

![Houston Texans Snap Counts Week 9](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/da7e5ac809ca2837958a87cdd6fa8f2de0fd090135ad3df545a34a4b780c4c1b/lightyear_networkapi/resizefill_w532_h782%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fhouston_texans_wire_usa_today_sports_articles_548%2Ff1fab4a1116134f7ded145e15a2c2921.png)

Houston Texans Snap Counts Week 9

Before the bye week, Dell was on a snap count. He was only expected to have about 12-16 snaps per contest. On Sunday, he recorded 33 snaps, which correlates to roughly 47% of all plays. Even if the ball wasn't going to him, he still showed that the knee could hold up in coverage.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Advertisement

New wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. was limited in his receptions, but it's become clear that the Texans plan on giving him a chance to prove his potential and a future No. 2 weapon opposite Nico Collins and Dell. He recorded 32 snaps, so roughly, he was out there for 46% of all plays.

As for the offensive line, no changes whatsoever, though Blake Fisher only saw action in the jumbo package of 7 snaps, a massive decrease from what fans have come to expect in the past. Among the running backs, Woody Marks, who led the team in rushing, finished with 46 snaps, while Dare Ogunbowale played in just 11 snaps, the second-fewest of any offensive player.

Case in point, Houston needs another running back to take the toll off Marks.

![Houston Texans Snap Counts Week 9](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/0061029188cafc0cf9c9cfe9b176ab684862b0eb555b1e6be48b182091a5c42c/lightyear_networkapi/resizefill_w636_h898%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fhouston_texans_wire_usa_today_sports_articles_548%2F079ed74e7af286adda450f67e51cc68c.png)

Houston Texans Snap Counts Week 9

## Defense

Perhaps the biggest change from last week's defensive outlook was the return of Jalen Pitre in the nickel. Not only did he record six tackles, including two for loss, but the do-it-all defensive back played in 96% of snaps. Rookie Kayden McDonald continued to see an uptick in his snap counts, totaling 24 snaps for a 33% ratio.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Advertisement

Regardless of health, Jadeveon Clowney is still playing more than just depth pieces. He finished with 24 snaps, which came out to be roughly 33% of the snaps. Both Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter only played in 44 snaps, but Anderson finished with a sack and two tackles for loss. Hunter, who has been quieter than usual this season, only recorded two tackles.

Meyers has spent most of the season as Cincinnati's third wide receiver behind [Ja'Marr Chase](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jamarr-chase/84270) and [Tee Higgins](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/tee-higgins/61211). [Andrei Iosivas](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/andrei-iosivas/109811) held that role in 2024, 2025 and the start of 2026, but he landed on injured reserve after Week 2 with a thumb injury that was expected to sideline him for four to six weeks. It has now been seven weeks, and there has been no word on when he will return to practice. Fourth-round rookie [Colbie Young](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/colbie-young/162739) was supposed to get the first opportunity to replace Iosivas, but he suffered a knee injury in Week 3. He returned to a limited role in Week 7 and more than doubled his snap count in Week 8. While Young didn't see a target in either game, he appeared to be a player on the rise. Young started this game in 11 personnel, but Meyers was on the field more often than not when the Bengals used that grouping. In the first half alone, Meyers recorded a 42-yard catch, a 16-yard run and a 5-yard reception. Meyers now has two career games with at least 60 offensive yards, while Iosivas has reached that mark just three times in 52 career games. Meyers could remain Cincinnati's third wide receiver even if Iosivas returns in the near future, and it's a role he could hold for multiple seasons. He could also become one of the top handcuff options at wide receiver if Chase or Higgins suffers an injury. **Falcons adjust without** [**Zachariah Branch**](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/zachariah-branch/174142) **:** The rookie didn't practice all week due to a hamstring injury and was ruled out on Friday. Atlanta has spent the season with [Drake London](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/drake-london/86519) as its lead receiver, [Jahan Dotson](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jahan-dotson/84375) and [Olamide Zaccheaus](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/olamide-zaccheaus/44920) as its other starters, [Chris Blair](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/chris-blair/84096) occasionally rotating in for Dotson and Branch rotating in for Zaccheaus. In recent weeks, Branch had started to draw even with Zaccheaus in playing time. Before this game, those were the only five wide receivers to play an offensive snap for Atlanta. The Falcons activated wide receiver [Beaux Collins](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/beaux-collins/144112) from injured reserve on Saturday. He was a full participant in practice all week after dealing with a hip injury. With Branch out, Dotson saw the biggest increase in snaps. Rather than rotating as frequently with Dotson, Blair began rotating with Zaccheaus. Zaccheaus saw a slight increase in snaps but not in his route participation rate. When Zaccheaus was off the field, it was often on third downs, with either Blair or Collins taking his place. It's unlikely that Branch, Zaccheaus, Blair or Collins will provide much fantasy value given how frequently they rotate. Dotson could have fantasy value, but only if Atlanta's offense performs better than it did in this game. ![](https://media.pff.com/2026/11/percentage_of_snaps_Jahan-Dotson-1024x731.png) **Miscellaneous Notes** - Atlanta running back [Brian Robinson Jr.](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/brian-robinson/57120) missed the past two games and was limited in practice all week with a hamstring injury. That didn't translate into much receiving production this week, as the wide receivers stole the show. * * * ### [Denver Broncos](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/denver-broncos/10) @ [Carolina Panthers](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/carolina-panthers/5) **Jonah Coleman takes the feature role for Denver:** Coleman played 58 offensive snaps, by far the most by a Broncos running back in a game since Sean Payton became head coach. Payton has been a head coach in the NFL for two decades, and throughout that time, he’s typically used a three-man running back rotation. This was true both in New Orleans and in Denver. Over the last two years, that rotation typically included [J.K. Dobbins](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/j.k.-dobbins/57366), [RJ Harvey](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/RJ-Harvey/99622/draft-profile) and [Tyler Badie](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/tyler-badie/83714). Last season, Dobbins missed the end of the year. In that time, Harvey became the lead back, but he topped out at playing two-thirds of the offensive snaps. Harvey and Badie are currently on injured reserve, while Coleman recently returned from IR. Coleman played 19-of-21 snaps in the second half last week, suggesting he would see a large role this week, but no one expected him to play 77% of the snaps. Dobbins rotated in at times on early downs, but Coleman dominated snaps in all other situations. Coleman only managed 3.4 yards per carry, but he scored a touchdown and caught four passes for 31 yards. We can expect his snap rate to decline slightly once either Badie or Harvey is able to return, as they would likely siphon some of the third-down or two-minute-drill snaps. As long as the [Broncos](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/denver-broncos/10) don’t trade for a running back at the trade deadline, then Coleman is likely safe for double-digit touches going forward, making him a fantasy starter in most matchups. Denver has its bye week next week, but then five of their final seven matchups during the fantasy season are favorable. Coleman is a buy-low option as long as Denver doesn’t acquire a running back. **Denver gains and loses a wide receiver:** [Pat Bryant](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/Pat-Bryant/144800/draft-profile) returned from injured reserve, but [Jaylen Waddle](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jaylen-waddle/84088) left with a concussion. Bryant spent the first three weeks of the season as the clear third receiver for Denver, playing 66% of snaps compared to 69% by [Jaylen Waddle](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jaylen-waddle/84088) and 79% by [Courtland Sutton](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/courtland-sutton/48164). His 86 yards during that time were more than Sutton’s 82. He left early in Week 4 and missed the following four weeks. In his absence, [Troy Franklin](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/troy-franklin/146567) was the Broncos' third receiver, playing 58% of snaps over the last four weeks. [Marvin Mims Jr.](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/marvin-mims-jr/122937) and [Lil’Jordan Humphrey](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/liljordan-humphrey/42247) also received an uptick in snaps. However, Franklin only caught four passes for 21 yards over those four games. With Bryant back, Humphrey was a healthy inactive. On the first two drives, Denver returned to its early-week rotation, with Sutton playing 16-of-23 snaps, Bryant 14 and Waddle 13, with Franklin and Mims rotating in at times, mostly on run plays rather than passes. Waddle departed after one play on the third drive. From that point, Sutton was rotated out much less than usual, playing 47-of-51 snaps. Bryant’s playing time wasn’t impacted, while Franklin was back to being the clear third receiver on the Denver depth chart. Bryant ended up leading the team in receiving production, catching four passes for 56 yards. Denver has its bye week next week, so there is a chance Waddle doesn’t miss any more time. Regardless, Bryant is a fine waiver-wire target, as he could be the Broncos' top receiving option over the rest of the season. If Denver’s offense improves, that could make him very valuable. ![](https://media.pff.com/2026/11/image-49-1024x731.png) **[Darren Waller](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/darren-waller/9637) dominates in a larger role:** Waller was the [Panthers](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/carolina-panthers/5)‘ primary source of offense, catching eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Carolina has used a three-man mix at tight end throughout the year, with [Tommy Tremble](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/tommy-tremble/84025) and [Mitchell Evans](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/MitcheLl-Evans/147486/draft-profile) playing in most 12 personnel sets, Waller appearing on third downs and Tremble leading the rotation in 11 personnel on early downs. Typically, whoever plays on third downs is the most fantasy-relevant of the group. Waller’s route participation rates have hovered between 40-60% all season. He played one early game with a 29% targets-per-route rate but had been under 14% in each of his other six outings. Waller had only caught two passes in his last three matchups. This week, Carolina shifted to using more 12 and 13 personnel, and less 11 personnel. Waller’s 12 personnel snap rate jumped from 30% to 50%. Waller’s snap mark was only a few percentage points higher than his season average. Yet his route participation figure was higher than usual, and most importantly, his target rate was also elevated. It’s fine to add Waller off the waiver wire, as there is a chance Carolina sees how well Waller played in this game and expands his role going forward. However, this could also be game-plan specific, and Carolina may return to its normal rotation, making Waller hard to rely on. ![](https://media.pff.com/2026/11/image-50-1024x731.png) **Miscellaneous Notes** - Carolina running back [AJ Dillon](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/aj-dillon/57165) was held out as a healthy scratch, his fourth straight absence. - [John Metchie III](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/john-metchie-iii/97400) remained the primary third wide receiver for Carolina in 11 personnel, but [Brycen Tremayne](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/brycen-tremayne/84425) ended up with more offensive snaps because he’s the principal receiver for Carolina in single-receiver sets. - Panthers tight end [Ja'Tavion Sanders](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jatavion-sanders/144717) was active after his seventh straight healthy scratch. He didn’t play an offensive snap. - The Broncos elevated running back [Cody Schrader](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/cody-schrader/157177) from the practice squad on Saturday. He was Denver’s third running back with [RJ Harvey](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/rj-harvey/99622) on injured reserve, similar to last week. * * * ### [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/dallas-cowboys/9) @ [Indianapolis Colts](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/indianapolis-colts/14) **[Cowboys](https://www.pff.com/nfl/teams/dallas-cowboys/9) adjust without** **[George Pickens](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/george-pickens/99229)** **:** The Cowboys' star receiver couldn't play due to a hamstring injury. He was limited all week and was ruled questionable on Friday. Dallas typically has a stable depth chart at wide receiver with [CeeDee Lamb](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/ceedee-lamb/61570) and Pickens as the top players, [Ryan Flournoy](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/ryan-flournoy/159617) as the third option in 11 personnel and [Kavontae Turpin](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/kavontae-turpin/47658) as the main backup. That hasn’t been the case in recent weeks, as Turpin has missed the last two games with a rib injury, while Pickens has been rotated out much more than usual because of his hamstring injury. This has led Flournoy to step up, with [Jonathan Mingo](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jonathan-mingo/97774) as the central backup. Turpin was out again this week, and Pickens joined him. With the two out, undrafted rookies [Camden Brown](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/camden-brown/157049) and practice squad call-up [Jordan Hudson](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jordan-hudson/157298) were the reserves. The Cowboys began the game with a predictable wide receiver rotation, with Lamb and Flournoy having 100% route participation rates into the third quarter. Mingo played 31 of the first 47 snaps of the game, but then he left with an ankle injury. He was initially ruled questionable, but he did not return. Brown was the only other receiver to play over the first eight drives with six snaps, mostly on run plays. He took over as the third receiver over the rest of the game. Dallas primarily stuck with 11 personnel, so Brown played in 22 of a possible 32 snaps over the rest of the game. Hudson only played one offensive snap. The injuries largely made Lamb even more of a focal point of the offense, as he caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. Flournoy’s increased playing time didn’t lead to elevated production, but he did catch two passes for 53 yards. If Pickens continues to miss time, then Flournoy is someone to keep in fantasy starting lineups. ![](https://media.pff.com/2026/11/image-55-1024x731.png) **Monitor** **[Jake Ferguson](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/jake-ferguson/61081)** **’s health:** Ferguson was questionable for this game with an ankle injury, and ended up leaving the matchup with a knee injury. Dallas has primarily used a two-man deplooyment at tight end between Ferguson and [Brevyn Spann-Ford](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/brevyn-spann-ford/84006). As time as progressed, Dallas has slowly but surely turned more toward Spann-Ford. [Luke Schoonmaker](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/luke-schoonmaker/84005) has been the Cowboys' third tight end, primarily playing in 13 personnel while taking some time from Ferguson in 12 personnel. He missed his second straight game with a groin injury. [James Mitchell](https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/james-mitchell/77885) was signed to the roster to take Schoonmaker’s place. Ferguson didn't practice on Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury but was limited in practice on Friday. He was questionable but was active. In the first half, the snap count between the two was pretty evenly split, with Spann-Ford handling 23 snaps and Ferguson 21. Ferguson generally stayed in for passing plays, while the Cowboys were more well-rounded when Spann-Ford was on the field. At one point in the first half, Ferguson was checked out in the blue medical tent. Ferguson left in the middle of the third quarter with a left knee injury. While he was able to walk to the sideline, he didn’t return to the game. Spann-Ford took all 21 snaps in the second half, with Mitchell joining him for five snaps out of 12 personnel. Spann-Ford caught two passes for 20 yards. His career-best outing is four receptions for 42 yards, and he has just one touchdown reception in his career. # "He Was Ready for His Moment": Why Tank Dell's Big Day Meant So Much to the Texans

Nov 09, 2026 at 08:32 AM

- Copied!

![_M__3631](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/texans/kj3spkqaqa8qvqds1ae7.jpg)

ALYSSA MULLIGAN/HOUSTON TEXANS

Stay on top of the latest Houston Texans news by adding [https://www.houstontexans.com](https://www.houstontexans.com/) to your Google Source Preferences.

WR Tank Dell went over 100 yards with a touchdown against the Chargers and earned a game ball. Head Coach DeMeco Ryans made sure all the credit went to Dell.

"All the credit goes to Tank, man, for the work that he put in. He was ready for his moment," Ryans said. "He's never short of confidence. He's a confident young man. He knows his ability. He believes in himself. He put the work in and he was ready for this opportunity."

### Tank Dell's Road Back

Ryans talked about the part of Dell's comeback that fans don't see.

"Even when you go through an injury like he suffered, there are a lot of dark days. There are a lot of difficult moments on the road to recovery. A lot of people don't see that. They see where he is right now," Ryans said. "Everybody on that sideline was really showing emotion and proud of the way Tank was able to come in and actually be an impact player for us, getting back to the plays that we're all used to seeing Tank make."

### C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell: The Connection Is Back

Ryans said the Texans saw the right look for Dell's big play and went for it.

"We knew we had the right look there with the cover, so we knew we wanted to get him," Ryans said. "Just credit to CJ first and foremost. The ball placement on that play was insane, outstanding ball placement to Tank. He just ran underneath it. Huge play. So proud of both guys getting that connection going. Excited to see how that continues to progress throughout the year."

QB C.J. Stroud talked about Dell's faith.

"I'm just super proud of him. He's been through a lot these last couple years, and just the perseverance, the faith that he has in God and where God has him in life," Stroud said. "To see him get a hundred, our second game back, off of a crazy injury like that, that's crazy. But for him, that's the type of confidence we have in Tank. He's a heck of a football player and showed it today."

### Tank Dell and C.J. Stroud: What to Know

**What does Stroud tell Dell?** "I try to tell him, like, man, I know I miss you sometimes, but just trust me, I got your back. I want the best for you. I want to see you succeed in life and in football," Stroud said. "So just to see him ball today was great. He's a great football player, and I'm really glad he's on our team."
